newsitem.title: INDIA: Mercedes Benz India to step up E-class car output.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes Benz India to step up E-class car output.

text.p: Mercedes Benz India Ltd said it is doubling its production to two shifts a day, with a provision to run a third shift if necessary, to support its aggressive marketing drive India and to cater for bulk export orders.
The company, a joint venture of Daimler-Benz AG and Tata Engieering and Locomotive Company Ltd (TELCO) assembles Mercedes E-class luxury cars in India.

"It is expected that this additional demand will exceed the company's ambitious targets for 1997 and necessitate a further import of 2,000 completely knocked down (CKD) kits from Germany," it said in a statement.
"This surge in demand follows the restructuring of its management and a a new marketing strategy which has placed particular emphasis on professional domestic marketing and exports," it said.
Mercedes said its expansion programme invoved establishment of new production facilities at Chiklin, near the western city of Pune, by end-1998.
Mercedes Benz India recently took over marketing of its cars from its partner TELCO, which is India's leading truck maker.

Mercedes said it planned to set up an efficient and exclusive dealer network throughout India with special focus on afer-sales service. The first exclusive Mercedes dealer showroom opened in Bangalore recently.
Till Becker, formerly managing director of Mercedes Benz Portugal, was recently appointed managing director and chief executive officer of the Indian firm.
